audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Kayle levels 2 and 3 and call levels 4-5 and 6 'Skill', while the whys in the same file say level 3 is the window to concede to the root and level 6 is where Kayle flips the lane.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Skill / Skill / Neeko / Kayle / Kayle / Kayle / Kayle, which matches the prose and the kit — Tangle-Barbs arriving at 3 is the only stretch Neeko owns against a melee Kayle, and everything from 6 onward is Kayle's.
audit.corrected: Row 1 -> Skill, row 2 -> Neeko, row 3 -> Kayle, row 4 -> Kayle; rows 0, 5, 6 unchanged. Flipped in matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly sited: Neeko level 3 (Tangle-Barbs), Kayle 6 (ranged Divine Ascent + Divine Judgment), Kayle first item, Kayle 2+ items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: the content layer never names a single Neeko ability — it says 'her E root', 'Q poke', 'W clone' throughout. No cooldowns are given either.
audit.why: Real names and numbers make the advice countable: Blooming Burst 9/8.5/8/7.5/7s, Tangle-Barbs 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 1000 range, Pop Blossom 120/105/90s. Riot's text also says Tangle-Barbs roots everything it passes through and grows larger, faster and longer-rooting after passing through a champion — so standing behind a teammate makes it worse, not safer.
audit.corrected: Named all five abilities in the prose, stated the 12s root cooldown as the trade trigger, and added the through-a-champion growth rule.

audit.why: Inherent Glamour breaking on immobilizing CC, on casting damaging spells and on damaging towers is correctly reflected by the existing warning about unwarded brush and disguised clones; nothing asserted beyond Riot's text.

edits.before: E-poke softens his step-ups while you scale. Only take the trade when Neeko's Tangle-Barbs is down.
edits.after: She has only Blooming Burst until Tangle-Barbs lands at 3 — trade even here, and sidestep the Q seed line.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Neeko must walk into your range.
edits.after: Tangle-Barbs comes online on a 12s cooldown and roots your melee form for her jungler — concede this window, farm at max range.

edits.before: Level 6 / 11 / 16 are the actual matchups — everything before is stalling. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Neeko's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Divine Ascent goes ranged and Divine Judgment blanks her Pop Blossom stun burst — the one combo that kills you does nothing for those seconds.

edits.before: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs: matchup-defining — Her root — extends through targets. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Neeko Tangle-Barbs: matchup-defining — 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s at 1000 range, and it grows after passing a champion. Dodge it, then step up. - Pop Blossom: 120/105/90s — answer it with your R. - Your ultimate: kill windows only.

edits.before: Neeko's window: with Q poke and E ready she can chunk your melee-range autos and root you in place for her jungler before your passive ever goes ranged.
edits.after: Neeko's window: Blooming Burst poke plus a 12s Tangle-Barbs root pins your melee form in place for her jungler, all before Divine Ascent goes ranged at 6.

edits.before: Neeko can't all-in and kill you the way a Renekton can, but her E root is the whole danger window — if she pins you in melee range she chunks you with Q poke and a passive proc, and worse, holds you in place for her jungler when you have no escape. Last-hit at max range, sidestep her Q skillshot line, and never walk into unwarded brush where a disguised W clone or her jungler could be waiting. Your W self-heal sustains you through her poke; just refuse to get rooted.
edits.after: Neeko can't all-in and kill you the way a Renekton can, but Tangle-Barbs is the whole danger window — a 12s root that pins you in melee range for Blooming Burst chip, and worse, holds you there for her jungler when you have no dash. Last-hit at max range and sidestep the Q seed line; never stand behind a teammate, because the tangle grows larger and roots longer after it passes a champion. Celestial Blessing sustains the poke; just refuse to get rooted.

notes: The whys array in the content layer is written one row out of step with the phase labels — whys[3] sits under 'Levels 4-5' but describes hitting level 6. The side flips proposed here follow the packet chart and leave the why text alone rather than compounding the offset; a human should decide whether the whys should be shifted down a row.
